title: Organismal Biology — Plant & Animal Organ Systems

days.title: Introduction to Organ Systems and Their Functions
days.content:
🎯 Learning Objectives

  • Identify the major organ systems in plants and animals.
  • Describe the primary function of each organ system.
  • Compare how plants and animals perform similar life processes.
  • Recognize that organ systems work together to maintain life.

🔑 Key Concepts

  • Organ System — a group of organs that work together to perform a specific function.
  • Organismal Biology — the study of structure, function, and behavior of whole organisms.
  • Homeostasis — maintenance of a stable internal environment.

📚 Lesson Content

A. Why Organ Systems Matter

Every living organism must perform the same fundamental life processes — but plants and animals do them in very different ways.

B. The Nine Life Processes We Compare

#ProcessAnimalsPlants
1ReproductionSexual & asexualSexual & asexual
2DevelopmentEmbryo → adultSeed → mature plant
3NutritionHeterotrophicAutotrophic
4Gas ExchangeLungs, gillsStomata, lenticels
5TransportHeart, blood vesselsXylem, phloem
6Body FluidsKidneysVacuoles, stomata
7ControlNervous, endocrineHormones
8ImmuneWBCs, antibodiesBarriers, chemicals
9Sensory/MotorEyes, musclesTropisms

C. Major Animal Organ Systems

SystemOrgansFunction
CirculatoryHeart, vessels, bloodTransport
RespiratoryLungs, trachea, gillsGas exchange
DigestiveMouth, stomach, intestinesBreakdown & absorb food
NervousBrain, spinal cord, nervesDetect & respond
EndocrineGlandsHormones
ExcretoryKidneys, bladderRemove wastes
Immune/LymphaticLymph nodes, WBCsDefense
ReproductiveGonadsOffspring
Muscular/SkeletalMuscles, bonesSupport, movement

D. Major Plant Organ Systems

SystemStructuresFunction
Shoot SystemLeaves, stems, flowersPhotosynthesis, reproduction
Root SystemRoots, root hairsAnchor, absorb water/minerals
Vascular SystemXylem, phloemTransport water, nutrients, sugars
Dermal SystemEpidermis, cuticleProtection, gas exchange

E. Comparative Preview

Today we set the stage. Over the next three days, we'll go deeper into how these systems work and how they maintain homeostasis — the body's internal balance.

days.title: Animal Organ Systems — Detailed
days.content:
🎯 Learning Objectives

  • Describe the major animal organ systems and their functions.
  • Explain how animal systems work together to maintain life.
  • Identify key organs of each system.
  • Explain how structure enables function in each system.

🔑 Key Concepts

  • Organ — a group of tissues that work together for a specific function.
  • System integration — organ systems coordinate for survival.
  • Surface-area-to-volume ratio — drives specialization in exchange surfaces.

📚 Lesson Content

A. Digestive System

  • Function: Break down food into absorbable nutrients
  • Organs: Mouth, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, liver, pancreas
  • Key adaptations: Villi and microvilli increase surface area

B. Circulatory System

  • Function: Transport nutrients, gases, hormones, wastes
  • Organs: Heart, blood vessels, blood
  • Types: Open vs closed

C. Respiratory System

  • Function: Exchange O₂ and CO₂
  • Organs: Lungs, trachea, bronchi, alveoli; gills in fish

D. Nervous System

  • Function: Detect stimuli and coordinate rapid responses
  • Organs: Brain, spinal cord, nerves

E. Endocrine System

  • Function: Secrete hormones for slower, longer-lasting regulation
  • Glands: Hypothalamus, pituitary, thyroid, adrenal, pancreas, gonads

F. Excretory System

  • Function: Remove metabolic wastes, regulate water/salt
  • Organs: Kidneys, ureters, bladder, urethra

G. Immune/Lymphatic System

  • Function: Defend against pathogens
  • Organs: Lymph nodes, spleen, thymus, tonsils, WBCs

H. Reproductive System

  • Function: Produce gametes for species survival
  • Organs: Gonads, ducts, accessory glands

I. Muscular & Skeletal Systems

  • Function: Support, movement, protection
  • Organs: Bones, cartilage, muscles, tendons, ligaments

scenarios.text: A person eats a meal and absorbs glucose.
Blood carries O₂ to muscles during exercise.
A person breathes faster on a run.
A reflex makes you pull your hand away from a hot stove.
Insulin is released after a sugary snack.
The bladder fills with urine.

questions.text: Which structure increases surface area for nutrient absorption in the small intestine?
Which system releases hormones to regulate body functions over long periods?
Which of the following correctly describes the excretory process?

takeaways: Each animal organ system has specialized organs for its function.
Structures are adapted to maximize efficiency (e.g., alveoli, villi).

days.title: Plant Organ Systems — Detailed
days.content:
🎯 Learning Objectives

  • Describe the shoot and root systems in plants.
  • Explain how xylem and phloem transport materials.
  • Describe the dermal system and its protective role.
  • Compare plant structural adaptations to those of animals.

🔑 Key Concepts

  • Shoot system — above-ground organs.
  • Root system — below-ground organs.
  • Vascular tissue — xylem (water) and phloem (sugars).
  • Dermal tissue — outer protective layer.

📚 Lesson Content

A. Shoot System

OrganFunctionAdaptations
LeavesPhotosynthesis, gas exchangeBroad surface; stomata; cuticle
StemsSupport, transportVascular bundles
FlowersReproductionAttract pollinators

B. Root System

  • Taproot: One main root (e.g., carrots)
  • Fibrous roots: Many thin roots (e.g., grasses)
  • Root hairs: Increase surface area for absorption

C. Vascular Tissue — Xylem & Phloem

TissueTransportsDirection
XylemWater and mineralsRoots → shoots
PhloemSugars and nutrientsBoth directions

D. Dermal Tissue

  • Epidermis: Outer layer
  • Cuticle: Waxy layer reducing water loss
  • Stomata: Pores for gas exchange

E. Plant vs Animal Adaptations

FunctionPlantsAnimals
Gas exchangeStomataLungs/gills
TransportXylem & phloemHeart & vessels
SupportCell walls, turgorSkeletal system

scenarios.text: Water moves from roots to leaves on a hot day.
Sugars are transported from leaves to growing roots.
A leaf closes its pores to save water.
A waxy layer prevents water loss.
A plant stores food in a thick underground root.
Root hairs absorb minerals from the soil.

questions.text: Which tissue transports water and minerals upward in plants?
What is the primary function of stomata?
Which structure increases surface area for water absorption?

takeaways: Plants have shoot and root systems.
Xylem transports water up; phloem transports sugars both ways.
The dermal system protects and controls gas exchange.

days.title: Comparative Processes — Reproduction, Nutrition, Gas Exchange
days.content:
🎯 Learning Objectives

  • Compare reproduction strategies in plants and animals.
  • Compare nutrition modes in plants and animals.
  • Compare gas exchange mechanisms.
  • Explain how each adaptation supports survival.

🔑 Key Concepts

  • Sexual vs asexual reproduction — genetic variation vs rapid multiplication.
  • Autotroph vs heterotroph — make own food vs consume others.
  • Diffusion surface — thin, moist, large surface for gas exchange.

📚 Lesson Content

A. Reproduction

AspectAnimalsPlants
SexualGametes → zygotePollination → seed
AsexualBudding, fragmentationRunners, tubers, bulbs
Advantage of sexualGenetic diversity → adaptation
Advantage of asexualFast, no mate required

B. Nutrition

AspectAnimalsPlants
ModeHeterotrophicAutotrophic
Source of carbonOrganic foodCO₂ from air
Energy sourceChemical energyLight energy
Key structuresMouth, digestive systemLeaves, chloroplasts, roots

C. Gas Exchange

AspectAnimalsPlants
OrgansLungs, gills, skinStomata, lenticels
O₂ intakeActive (breathing)Passive (diffusion)
CO₂ releaseExhaleDiffuse through stomata

D. Why These Differences?

  • Animals are motile → need active systems.
  • Plants are sessile → rely on diffusion and environment.
  • Each group's structures reflect its environmental niche.

scenarios.text: Produces seeds after pollination.
Uses hemoglobin to carry oxygen in blood.
Absorbs CO₂ through stomata.
Uses gills or lungs for gas exchange.
Has an autotrophic mode of nutrition.
Can reproduce asexually.

questions.text: Which statement correctly compares nutrition in plants and animals?

choices.label: Plants are autotrophic; animals are heterotrophic
Plants are heterotrophic; animals are autotrophic

questions.text: How does gas exchange differ between plants and animals?

choices.label: Animals use active breathing via lungs/gills; plants use passive diffusion through stomata
Plants use lungs; animals use stomata

questions.text: Which mode of reproduction provides genetic diversity in both plants and animals?

takeaways: Plants and animals perform the same life processes but with different structures.
Animals use active systems; plants rely on diffusion.
Reproduction can be sexual or asexual in both groups.
Nutrition: animals are heterotrophs; most plants are autotrophs.
